title: Do Sellers Benefit from Sponsored Product Listings? Evidence from an Online Marketplace
authors: Mingyu Joo; Jiaqi Shi; Vibhanshu Abhishek
main_or_robustness: main (listing-level click/conversion logits of sponsored vs organic listings with query-product FE; no time dimension)

ineligible_specs.reported_location: Section 4.3 main tables (click and conversion tendency by position)
ineligible_specs.exclusion_reason: cross-sectional logit (bife) of clicked/buynow on sponsored x position-cluster with query-product FE; no adoption timing, no calendar-time FE, nonlinear

eligible_reason: Not a DiD. Sponsored vs organic listings are compared within query-product cells across ad positions in search-impression data; there is no staggered adoption and no time dimension.
design_notes: Mechanism splits by Nelson search/experience categories and rating; ROI back-of-envelope in Section 5.
data_files_note: 17% random sample of the impression data; DVs synthesized, ratings disguised, IDs anonymized (readme.docx).
data_provenance_note: readme.docx: 'Dependent variables are synthesized to disguise the actual numbers of clicks/conversions'; high_rating 'true values disguised'.
screener_notes: No article text available; design read from readme and 2.Sponsored_listings_model.R. Article text and OpenAlex abstract unavailable (INFORMS abstracts withheld); package_mismatch checked against title and authors.
